statement: Let A = ef J0(N) have the normalization (C1). Suppose K has odd fundamental discriminant −D < −4, splitting 2N, and L(f/K, s) 110 has a simple zero at 1. Use S above finite rational primes splitting in K, including 2N in the prime-support sense, archimedean places understood, and eS for the omission multiplier of f over Q. Put P = ef PX on A(K)Q for the Hilbert trace of (GZ). Over K consider the complex C∗ on M∗. Fix one of the two primes w | 2, impose the strict condition there, and impose full conditions at every other finite prime of the support, including w̄. Then C∗ is rationally acyclic and its characteristic determinant has valuation −d(C∗, 1) = 2v2(eS logω,w P). (C-pair) The differential in this identity is the normalized newform differential, as in (M3).
